gloss: to look toward; to pay attention to

definitions.gloss: to look toward; to pay attention to
definitions.explanation: To turn one's gaze toward something, or to show interest in something. Most commonly used in the negative form 見向きもしない (to not even glance at, to completely ignore).

examples.japanese: {誰|だれ}も{見向|みむ}きもしなかった。
あの{店|みせ}は{客|きゃく}に{見向|みむ}きもされない。
examples.english: That shop is completely ignored by customers.

examples.japanese: {安|やす}い{商品|しょうひん}には{見向|みむ}きもせず、{高級品|こうきゅうひん}ばかり{買|か}う。
examples.english: Without even glancing at cheap products, they only buy luxury items.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used in the negative pattern 見向きもしない, meaning "to not pay the slightest attention to" or "to completely ignore." The affirmative form is rarely used.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見向|みむ}きもしない (to not even glance at)
- {見向|みむ}きもされない (to be completely ignored)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {無視|むし}する: to ignore — a more direct and common word for ignoring
- {振|ふ}り{向|む}く: to turn around — to physically turn to look
